dy.x: The word dy is a particle used in composition before adjectives, to make them adverbs, as nearly every adjective can be made an adverb by placing dy before it., For sake of abridging the work I have only inserted a few, yet the reader may understand how they are made, by the following | that or there., I think this word, as used in composition, to be adverbial; as in er aggle dy bee (lest that); er aggle dy beagh (for fear that be); or (for fear there be); dy row (that was); (there was); (that be); (be as that); | to;, when placed before verbs is always to; as, dy aagail (to leave); dy aarlaghey (to cook); dy arraghey (to shift); &c.; pronounced dhe | if;, dy beagh eh (if he were); dy raghin, or, as it is spoken, dy rhoin (if I went); dy n'aasagh oo mooar (if thou wouldst grow big) | of, when placed before substantives, as, lane dy arroo (full of corn); laad dy ooir (a load of earth); kuse dy hollan (a quantity of salt), &c.; there may be exceptions nevertheless; as, veih boayll dy boayl, [1]
